missingTests.title: No unit test for findActivePod / filterActivePods selection semantics
missingTests.body: The new findActivePod helper and the refactored filterActivePods are exercised only indirectly by the e2e scenarios. The very property this PR fixes — that selection must skip terminal/terminating pods and never return one — is not asserted anywhere. A focused table-driven unit test over findActivePod (mixed terminal/active/deleting pods, all-terminal → nil, ordering-independence) would pin the predicate behavior and regress cheaply if IsPodActive semantics ever drift. The e2e path cannot reliably assert the non-deterministic-selection property because the list contents at the selection point are themselves non-deterministic.
missingTests.evidence: findActivePod (restart_policy_stability.go:654-661) and filterActivePods (:636-645) have no _test.go coverage; PR body section IV states 'No standalone unit test file is added; the helper is covered by the e2e scenarios.'
missingTests.why: The fix's correctness rests entirely on findActivePod returning an active pod and nil otherwise. Without a direct test, a future change to the predicate (or a different IsPodActive definition after a k8s upgrade) could silently reintroduce the flake with no unit-level signal.

optionalImprovements.title: findActivePod and filterActivePods duplicate the IsPodActive iteration
optionalImprovements.body: nit: findActivePod and filterActivePods each open-code the `for i := range pods { if kubecontroller.IsPodActive(...) }` loop. One could delegate to the other (e.g. findActivePod returns &filterActivePods(pods)[0]) so there is a single source of truth for 'active' selection. The current form is fine and avoids an allocation; only worth it if you prefer one predicate site.
optionalImprovements.evidence: filterActivePods (:636-645) and findActivePod (:654-661) both iterate pods calling kubecontroller.IsPodActive.

optionalImprovements.title: findActivePod returns a pointer aliasing the input slice
optionalImprovements.body: nit: findActivePod returns &pods[i], a pointer into the caller's slice backing array. All current callers pass a fresh PodList.Items and do not mutate it afterwards, so this is safe today. A one-line note in the doc comment ('returns a pointer into pods; callers must not mutate the slice while holding it') would keep it safe as the helper gets reused.
optionalImprovements.evidence: findActivePod returns &pods[i] (line 660). Callers: runRestartPolicyRecreateTest, runRestartPolicyNoneReplaceTest, runRestartBackoffDelayTest (x2), runRestartBackoffSpecChangeTest (x2).
